target_customer: Couples and close friends, mostly young consumers on mobile who pay for a premium subscription
problem: Relationships drift through missed check ins and shallow talk. Candle gives pairs a short daily game, shared widgets and streaks to build connection.

founders.name: Alex Ruber
prior_employers: NASA JPL (flight systems and sequencing engineer)
previous_startups: Encore (AI shopping app, co-founder, pivoted into Candle)

founders.name: Parth Chopra
previous_startups: Encore (AI shopping app, co-founder, pivoted into Candle)

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile content and widget app with streaks and photo sharing is standard consumer engineering with no hard technical barrier.

defensibility.rationale: Shared memories and streaks create some lock in between a pair, but similar apps (Paired, Couply and others) are easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Paired and other couples apps exist per 2026 comparison sites; no source shows them copying or buying Candle.

market_need_then: Couples apps already had paying users, and TechCrunch reports Candle reached 300,000 users and over 1M ARR within six months of the pivot in 2025, evidence of demand.

identity.mascot_or_character: Friendly flame mascot per an app showcase site
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and low pressure, described by users as not cringe

branding.brand_signature: The Duolingo for Relationships positioning with a flame mascot
branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch says growth relies on a creator led TikTok and Instagram engine and a viral TikTok from a team member.

brand_strength.rationale: Warm evocative name and mascot fit the product and creator led social growth worked, but the common word is generic and several apps share the name.

pivots.from: Encore, an AI shopping tool (after several earlier ideas)
pivots.why: TechCrunch reports the shopping app's unit economics did not work; the founders pivoted five times before Candle

outcome_analysis: Candle is the result of a pivot from an AI shopping app that worked technically but not economically. After the switch the couples app reached about 300,000 users and over 1M ARR in six months through creator led social growth, and its site later claims over a million users. Competition from established couples apps and low switching barriers are risks.
notes: TechCrunch says the earlier Encore raised about 2M USD with backers Goodwater Capital, Pioneer Fund, Progression Fund and Y Combinator; those belong to the predecessor project, not recorded as Candle rounds because stage and date are not given. YC lists founded year 2025 though the batch is Fall 2024. No competitor source dated near the batch was found (comparison pages are from 2026), so the list is empty. The 1 million user figure is self reported by the company site.
